extracted.intended_audience: secondary-school English teachers and educators designing classroom writing projects (esp. health education/HIV-awareness)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running a task-based classroom project in which high‑school students collaboratively write a proposal to raise awareness of HIV/AIDS in their community, using workshops, community input, and a UNICEF model as scaffolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task-based writing project
rubrics_metrics.description: This article describes a task-based writing project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a real, goal-oriented writing task (writing a community proposal) rather than isolated exercises; framing the activity as a meaningful task helps drive student engagement and language use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: proposal to raise community HIV/AIDS awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Students wrote a proposal to raise awareness of HIV/AIDS in their community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project should have a clear, public-facing purpose (health awareness) so student work is authentic and aimed at a real audience and social goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to students' lives
rubrics_metrics.description: By writing on a topic related to their lives, students were motivated and empowered to use their English skills for positive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose topics connected to students' experiences to increase motivation and the perceived value of language learning; relevance is an explicit criterion for topic selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive workshop format
rubrics_metrics.description: The project was an interactive workshop that invited a community leader to help with brainstorming, the setting of ground rules, and understanding of the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the lesson as an interactive workshop rather than a lecture; include activities such as brainstorming and explicit ground-rule setting to scaffold group work and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community stakeholder involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited a community leader to help with brainstorming, the setting of ground rules, and understanding of the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring external/community voices into the classroom to provide authentic perspectives, help frame the issue, and contribute to idea generation and norms for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative drafting and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Students worked together on their responses and drafted and revised a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize collaborative composition processes and iterative revision (draft -> revise) as core parts of the project; group work and peer feedback are central quality‑improvement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established model/template (UNICEF model)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal was based on a model from UNICEF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide students with a recognized template or model to scaffold structure and content (e.g., UNICEF model) so they can focus on language and persuasive/content choices within a clear framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language learning as empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Students were motivated and empowered to use their English skills for positive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess success not only by linguistic accuracy but also by whether the project enabled students to use language to advocate or effect change; empowerment is an intended learning outcome.
